data.name: HelpText
data.value: Choose a display from the list, or click it in the arrangement, to change its settings. Drag a display to move it; it snaps against the others, so there are never gaps between screens. Nothing changes until you click Apply. After applying you have 15 seconds to keep the new settings; if you do nothing, the old ones come back, so a mode that leaves the screen blank undoes itself.

data.name: Waiting
data.value: Waiting for the window system to describe the displays...

data.name: AdaptiveSyncUnsupported
data.value: This display does not support adaptive sync.

data.name: HdrUnsupported
data.value: This display does not support HDR.

data.name: SdrWhiteTip
data.value: How bright ordinary (SDR) white is while the display is in HDR. Lower it if the desktop looks brighter than the screens beside it.

data.name: NoCompositor
data.value: The window system does not offer display configuration, or is not running.

data.name: ApplyFailed
data.value: The window system refused these settings. Nothing was changed.

data.name: ApplyCancelled
data.value: The displays changed while these settings were being applied. Nothing was changed; check the settings and apply again.

data.name: RevertFailed
data.value: The previous settings could not be restored.

data.name: DisplaysChanged
data.value: A display was connected or disconnected, so the settings were reloaded.

data.name: RevertingIn
data.value: The previous settings come back in {0} seconds.

data.name: NightLightIntro
data.value: Night light makes the colors on every screen warmer, which is easier on the eyes after dark.

data.name: NightLightTemperatureTip
data.value: The color temperature at night. Lower is warmer; 6500 K is daylight, which is no change. While you move this, the screen shows the new color for a few seconds.

data.name: NightLightUseTimeZoneTip
data.value: Work out sunset and sunrise for the city the system time zone is named after. Turn this off to give your own latitude and longitude.

data.name: NightLightHelpText
data.value: Night light warms the colors of every screen. Choose Always on, or Sunset to Sunrise to have it fade in as the sun goes down and out again in the morning. The slider sets how warm the screen gets; the screen shows each new color for a few seconds as you move it. Sunset and sunrise are worked out for your time zone's location unless you give a latitude and longitude. Changes on this page take effect at once; Reset puts back what was set when the window opened. Screenshots are not affected.

data.name: NightLightUnsupported
data.value: The settings service on this system does not have night light settings yet. Update wlrix-settings-daemon and the window system, then log in again.
